projects.name: ATLAS
projects.oneLine: Topology-aware learned attention over spatial memory for indoor UAV exploration.
projects.statusLabel: Draft results · KTH benchmark + preliminary aerial simulation
projects.honesty: Draft results from ATLAS_v1. KTH evaluates exploration per unit of motion, excluding planning time and the aerial camera, shield and flight controller. Aerial baseline comparisons, ablations and decision-cost measurements are pending; current-policy hardware validation is not reported.
projects.whatItDoes: ATLAS chooses where an indoor UAV should explore next. It retains observed geometry in a metric map and place graph, keeps a separate token for each current candidate, and reads the remaining places through a fixed bank of learned queries. Graph topology and full-graph route lengths inform goal selection. In aerial execution, each motion prefix is checked against observed free space and a reactive depth shield can stop the drone.
projects.commitment: Retain spatial memory. Learn goal selection. Check motion geometrically.
designPoints: Keep the full measured map and place graph; compress the policy readout without pruning remembered places.
Bias candidate attention with graph adjacency, shared free-space components and distance.
Train whole-goal forecasts across replanning; exclude abandoned, unresolved goals from forecast targets.
Keep learned predictions outside the measured map and geometric safety checks.

media.heroNote: Selected KTH floor-plan benchmark replays; accelerated playback.

method.heading: How ATLAS chooses its next goal

items.title: Persistent memory, compact readout
items.text: Every current candidate keeps its own token. A bank of 64 learned queries reads the other remembered places. For a fixed candidate count, attention cost grows linearly with remembered places; candidate attention remains quadratic in the number of candidates. This is an architectural cost statement, not a measured end-to-end speed result.

items.title: Topology-aware candidate attention
items.text: Graph adjacency, shared free-space components and distance bias attention between candidates. Route descriptors computed on the full graph retain information about paths through remembered places. Local and global map tokens are fused with the graph representation and recurrent state.

items.title: Forecast the whole goal
items.text: The network predicts duration, newly observed area and probability of reaching each goal. These forecasts inform the actor. When replanning keeps the same goal, observed segments are joined into one target; abandoned unresolved goals receive no forecast target.

items.title: Distillation and reinforcement learning
items.text: The compact policy is distilled from an earlier dense-attention policy and then fine-tuned with PPO using duration-aware advantages. The evaluated policy uses collected trajectories only. The auxiliary graph model was fitted with the encoder frozen; imagined actor–critic updates were not enabled.

items.title: Independent motion checks
items.text: Aerial motion prefixes, including turning and stopping envelopes, must stay within observed free space. A separate 5 cm local grid supports swept-body checks, and a reactive depth shield guards execution between checks. These aerial safety components are outside the KTH floor-plan benchmark.

projects.hypothesis: The remaining experiments test aerial performance against FALCON, EDEN, CogniPlan and ARiADNE, isolate the contribution of each policy component, and measure complete decision cost as the map grows.
contribution: Developed ATLAS for goal selection with topology-aware attention over persistent spatial memory.
Trained the compact policy through distillation and reinforcement learning, and evaluated it on KTH floor plans and preliminary aerial simulation scenes.

evidence.heading: Results in the new draft
paragraphs: Average observable-floor coverage across all 14 KTH floors is 80.36% for ATLAS, compared with 38.74% for CogniPlan and 42.33% for ARiADNE. The shared setting uses a 0.30 m body with 0.05 m padding per face, 8 m sensing and an 1800 s motion budget. Four starts are averaged within each floor, then the 14 floors are weighted equally. This aggregate is not the result of a single video run. Planning time is excluded.

The area under the observable-coverage curve is 0.719 for ATLAS, 0.377 for CogniPlan and 0.413 for ARiADNE. ATLAS is ahead on this measure on all 14 floors, but complete exploration remains uncommon: only 2 of 56 ATLAS episodes reach 99% observable coverage.

Preliminary aerial simulation reports mean newly observed areas of 1714 m² in the school and 1999 m² in the research wing, each from two scored starts using the full 1800 s budget. No collision was recorded in the reported preliminary runs. These are development scenes, some starts remain unfinished, and no aerial baseline comparison is yet available.
Source: ATLAS_v1 draft, Section VI, Tables III–IV and Figure 8. These draft findings do not establish real-flight performance or end-to-end planning speed.

overview.sourceNote: Updated from Bavantha_CV.pdf, Saxion application, 7 September 2026. This overview reflects the current CV; detailed project pages retain their existing technical descriptions.
overview.intro: I build perception, mapping and navigation systems for robots, from the first model to deployment. These projects span my PhD research, commercial robotics and the work that got me started.

groups.label: 01 / Thesis research
groups.title: Structuring the Seen, Exploring the Unseen
groups.intro: Monocular perception, 3D mapping and learned exploration, brought together on a custom drone.

items.name: Mono-Hydra++
items.text: I built a monocular scene-graph mapping system that combines learned perception with visual-inertial estimation. Sparse predicted-depth factors anchor the pose estimate, while predictions are aligned across frames before fusion. The ROS 2 stack runs on the drone’s Jetson Orin NX with a ZED X One camera.

items.name: M2H / M2H-MX
items.text: I designed how depth, semantics, surface normals and edges share information in one network. M2H uses DINOv2 with windowed cross-task attention; M2H-MX adds LoRA-adapted DINOv3 features and register-gated Mamba context. They provide the perception front end for Mono-Hydra++.

items.name: ATLAS
items.status: Draft results · KTH benchmark + preliminary aerial simulation
items.text: ATLAS selects exploration goals with topology-aware learned attention over persistent spatial memory. The draft reports KTH floor-plan benchmarks and preliminary aerial simulation runs.

groups.note: The earlier Mono-Hydra system established the monocular mapping pipeline in 2023.

groups.label: 02 / Commercial robotics
groups.title: Humanoid visitor guidance & interaction
groups.intro: I built the navigation software and led deployments of more than 30 robots for over 10 enterprise clients, including Expo 2020 Dubai.

items.name: Robots working with the public
items.text: I integrated ROS and GMapping navigation, LiDAR and 3D obstacle sensing with robot SDKs and voice assistance. As the founding robotics engineer and later a three-engineer team lead, I worked on site to get the robots navigating and interacting reliably around visitors.

groups.label: 03 / Undergraduate research
groups.title: Autonomous reconnaissance robot
groups.intro: My first exploration and mapping project, built in a three-student team.

items.name: Mapping an unknown environment
items.text: I developed the SLAM system, combining 2D LiDAR mapping with stereo vision for object geometry. The project produced three papers and received the IESL Best Undergraduate Project and IET Sri Lanka Best Technical Paper awards.

platform.text: A custom quadrotor carrying a ZED X One camera and a Jetson Orin NX 16GB. M2H-MX inference is exported through ONNX and optimised with TensorRT FP16.
